name: rfmem
description: Wraps RF-Mem (Applied-Machine-Learning-Lab/ICLR2026_RF-Mem, ICLR 2026, "Evoking User Memory: Personalizing LLM via Recollection-Familiarity Adaptive Retrieval"): an adaptive retrieval strategy inspired by dual-process memory theory -- a cheap probe retrieval's mean similarity/entropy decides whether to take a fast 'Familiarity' path (direct top-k similarity search) or a slower 'Recollection' path (iterative beam search with KMeans re-clustering and MMR diversity re-ranking at each level, re-embedding the query toward each cluster's centroid). Family A/C boundary case: retrieval-only, no LLM-driven fact extraction at ingestion time (embeddings only, via dialogue_benchmarks.llm.embed()) -- the entire retrieval decision and both paths run with zero LLM calls, confirmed by reading upstream's own main pipeline directly (a HyDE query-expansion helper exists in the source but is dead code, never called by the actual 'RF-Mem' retrieval_mode). Only the final answer-generation step (given the retrieved chunks) goes through dialogue_benchmarks.llm.complete(), same as bm25_rag/dense_rag. No repository-level LICENSE file (README claims MIT, GitHub API reports license: None) -- used for internal reproduction only, per the same resolution applied to pathrag/orig/sbys/lmedr/memalpha this session. Vendored and adapted (vendor/rf_mem.py) since no PyPI package exists; upstream's own target datasets (LongMemEval/PersonaBench/PersonaMem) have no adapter in this repo yet, so this Method targets any session-grouped or flat-turn conversation shape already supported here (locomo, msc, personachat, ...). See method.py's module docstring for what was adapted vs. kept verbatim, and the confirmed-dead dependencies dropped at vendor time.
